answer: Every transaction needs countersignatures from randomly assigned verifiers whose stake is locked on-ledger; if a countersigned transaction is proven invalid, that stake is burned automatically by the protocol. Verification authority comes from staked capital, not identity, so fake identities earn nothing, and each forgery costs more than an entire epoch of rewards, making fraud structurally unprofitable.
